Online Love Scams

By: Michael Duffett | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Can we all be susceptible to online love scams?

Unique Selling Point:
As we become more isolated by social media, we become even more needy for intimacy - hence the prevlance of dating sites, chat rooms etc. All over the world there had been a huge increase of internet lovescams. More often than not, conmen approach women online via dating sites, facebook and an online relationship is started - there is always a promise that the couple will meet, but it never happens - So convincing are these conmen are that they are able to get the women to give them money - usualy its for some fake medical emergency - often these conmen say they are on oil rigs, or in the army stationed at the other side of then worrld. fake pictures are used to lure the women. We interview the women who have been scammed and hear from them how it is possible that they lost all their money to the conman? What was going on in their minds? Too often the public will say - these women are stupid. This program wants to change that narrative. As one forensic psychiatrist said - its astutely arrongant to take on that kind of thinking...its aggorant to think none of us can be conned!!!!

Summary:
Three good case studies - Louis who was conned out of 5 million rand. She was devestated as she lost everything.She had to live in a back room. She started an online NGO and she spends all her time, for no money, trying to prevent women from being scammed. `She has 5000 followers. Then there is Zelda, aged 59, who lost R600 000 to a man she thought was a 31 year old man in the USA Army in Afghanistan. Actually he is a Nigerian living in Cape Town, and a private detective had been able to identify him through tracking down the mule who collected money for him. We hope to set a trap and confront him. And then there is Lana who fell in love with a man she thought was on a rig off the coast of Scotland. We have his voice recordings and a picture of this man - a boemelaar living in Kemptom Park - set up by Nigerians. Lana lost R500 000.

Further information:
A forensic psychiatrist will come onto the program and we have invited SAPS and the Hawks to appear as well. We wont to know what the protocol is - for we hear that many who have bgeen scammed and who try and report it to local police stations are turned away because the cops say they freely gave away the money. Not so, in terms of the Criminal Procedue Act - IT IS FRAUD. This must be stressed on the program. is there any specialised unit involved in tracking down these crooks or is it left to the detectives at each branch? The Hawks did make a bust last year in a cooperative venture between themslves and the FBI. Maybe they can come onto the program?

Press Release:


Online Love Scams
With Valentine’s Day around the corner, and desperate to find love, some internet users turn to online dating. But beware – scammers are preying on lonely hearts, making off with millions in the process. Carte Blanche examines the psychology behind why some singles still fall for dating scams, which leave them destitute.
Producer: Michael Duffett | Presenter: Masa Kekana


Script:


The 64 year old Gauteng woman, we will call her Anita as she did not want her
identity to be revealed was thrilled when she found love online. Her husband
had passed away 7 years earlier.
Anita
I met Ramstoen Vand Hof and we spoke for a long time.
VO
She adored his looks and the messages she constantly received from him
Sound up: I really really care about you and I have strong feelings.
VO
She had no idea that pictures he sent was actually of Greek politician and that
she was about to become another victim of an online romance scam:. She fitted
the perfect profile : lonely caring kind and trusting

Link
scammers target their victims on Facebook Instagram Linkedin Whatsapp
and many dating sites particularly targeting middle aged women many of
whom are not so tech savvy.

VO
It’s on the dating app Tinder that Anita met her south African so called lover.
She was overjoyed when he promised to marry her when returned home from
Scotland where he did contract work. The romance gathered momentum.
ANITA
he said that he would like to hold me and also smear cream over me after a
shower.
VO
But Anita never had eye to eye contact with him and this is one of the reasons
why these scams occur, according to forensic psychiatrist Dr. Larissa Panieri
ANITA Peter: Love messages create fantasies
Psychiatrist
In a short space of time you actually must believe that those things are the
reality. So it becomes easier and easier for the person doing the con to actually
convince you of whatever it is because you want to be convinced at some level
you want to believe that you want to believe this person loves you in this
magical way that nobody else would understand.
V0
After 4 months, Anita’s so called internet lover stared requiting money . she
believed him when he said that he would pay her back when he receievd money
owed to him. First it was airtime, then he needed money to pay his attorneys to
sort out his taxes……the requests kept coming.. When sometimes she hesitated
to transfer funds, he manipulated her
ANITA
he would get cross with me and say that I don’t like me and he said that he was going to marry me, and buy me a house
vO
Over a nine month period, Anita transferred every cent she owned - a total of
R500 00 . Then her world was shattered. It transpired that all along she was
actually speaking to a homeless person who had been set up by a syndicate in
South Africa to be part of the deception. It was the rejection from her family
that affected her the most. She recalls the time when she tried to speak to her
sister daughter.
I
ANITA
Once I contracted my sister, she said leave my daughter out of this, we don’t
want to see you again or talk to you..

VO
It is the grooming and manipulation by scammers that lure victims as capetonian
Louis Haynes found out the hard way. She was also lonely and found romance
online. She felt safe enough to share with this man, whom she thought was an
American, the grief she experienced when her six month old daughter died of
whooping cough.
LOUIS
When I walked into the ICU I saw the machine…You know that she is dying.
And then I left everything and ran to her and I picked up and he died in my
arms.
VO
It was a full six months before her scammer requested money and Louise used
MoneyGram and western union to transfer funds. She was delighted when he
said that he wanted to fly to South Africa with his two children to meet her. But
then she got a desperate message from him.
LOUIS
on their way to the airport. They were in a very bad accident and his children
were in ICU. They will die if they don't get the - he said I know you lost a
child can you please help me.You can just think what is going through my mind
at the moment because you know I don't want another child death
VO
Louise without hesitation transferred 600000 Rand to him but that's the last she
heard from him. In total she had given him eight hundred thousand rand. She
was devastated and it took her a long time to recover.
PRESENTER
How were you feeling during that period?
LOUIS
You feel lonely you feel the place you feel suicidal you feel ashamed.
VO
But Louis fought back and she started an NGO called Sky Woman to educate
women about these scams.
LOUIS
We support women. We know we understand because we were s victims.

VO
One desperate person who contacted Sky Woman for help was Petro SWART
who was living in a shelter after losing all her money to a scammer. Her
husband, a pastor, had recently died.
PRESENTER
Take me through how you felt after your husband passed away.

PETRO
I was lonely. I wanted that love that I had for 25 years because he was smiling.
It was my love of my life.
VO
She joined Instagram when she began a conversation with this man
she though was in Europe. She fell head over heels in love with him
Petro
I felt like I was in another world. All the promises all the nice things you said
to me and all the things he promised me. It was like a real voodoo spell he had
on me.
VO
It would be a full nine months before her scammer stated to ask for money..
He said that his bank account had been frozen. He made up a story that his
daughter had been seriously injured and urgent finds were required for her
medical expenses. Petra who was obsessed with this relationship obliged.
PSYCHIATRIST
It becomes like all consuming addiction it holds you there and it's got love
involved. That's firing the centers of our brain that hold us captive. It is possible
that that is why she keeps up with that. Just like a gambler keeps giving his
money until he's gone. Just like a person who uses heroin keeps with the heroin
until they're in the gutter.
VO
That’s exactly what happened to Petro. By the time she realized that she was
being scammed she had lost everything - R800000 Rand .
PETRO
I felt like I was raped. I was suicidal. I actually tried twice to take my life

VO
Touched by story, Louise and Zelda Erasmus who also worked for Sky woman
rescued Petro from the shelter and helped relocate HER to Riviersonderend, a
two hour drive from Cape Town - where they found her accommodation. Zelda
had also been a victim losing R600000 to this man she met online who said that
he was an American soldier living in Afghanistan. She took it on the chin
though
ZeLDA
I made a mistake, its no good being devastated about it, if I get depressed how
am I going to do my work
VO
John alexander, a Cape Town private investigator, was also touched by the
victims’ stories AND decided to help them.
JOHN
Bear in mind this is females in their 50s 60s even 70s that lost absolutely
everything. At one point in their life they were quite successful at least the
majority of them and now all of a sudden they're lost literally everything.
VOICE OVER
Within a few days he discovered the identity of Zelda’S scammer. He is foreign
national living THE high life in Cape Town. He's also identified the mules in
Anita’ case -THESE were the people who collected her money AT money market cash points
on behalf of her scammer..
JOHN
At this stage they stole out there and that's also a case we're willing to give over
to the TPC for further investigation
VO
Brigadier Venese Naidu national spokesman for South African Police Services
said he would welcome the information from Alexander and said that his team
would work on this with the National prosecuting authority should it fall within
their mandate..

VO
In the meantime Petra is slowly recovering and keeps busy by helping prepare
food for a nearby market. Louis is working hard to change perceptions because
she feels that victims are unfairly ridiculed for falling prey to scammers. Lious’s
mission is to try and prevent women from becoming victims but Dr Panieri
Peter knows this wont always be possible.
Psychiatrist
I think intimacy clouds most peopl;s judgment so real all falsely perceived
intimacy is something which is designed to make you not think very clearly
about other things. When one is in love with somebody in person or online that
tends to be the overriding thing. the nature of love. It is why we love it.

As one forensic psychiatrist said - its astutely arrongant to take on that kind of thinking...its aggorant to think none of us can be conned!!!!
metadata.Summary: Three good case studies - Louis who was conned out of 5 million rand. She was devestated as she lost everything.She had to live in a back room. She started an online NGO and she spends all her time, for no money, trying to prevent women from being scammed. `She has 5000 followers. Then there is Zelda, aged 59, who lost R600 000 to a man she thought was a 31 year old man in the USA Army in Afghanistan. Actually he is a Nigerian living in Cape Town, and a private detective had been able to identify him through tracking down the mule who collected money for him. We hope to set a trap and confront him. And then there is Lana who fell in love with a man she thought was on a rig off the coast of Scotland. We have his voice recordings and a picture of this man - a boemelaar living in Kemptom Park - set up by Nigerians. Lana lost R500 000.
metadata.Further information: A forensic psychiatrist will come onto the program and we have invited SAPS and the Hawks to appear as well. Not so, in terms of the Criminal Procedue Act - IT IS FRAUD. This must be stressed on the program. is there any specialised unit involved in tracking down these crooks or is it left to the detectives at each branch?
